33	
34	All request and response bodies are JSON. Unknown fields are rejected.
35	
36	### Health
37	
38	```http
39	GET /health
40	```
41	
42	Returns `{"status":"ok"}`.
43	
44	### Create a workflow
45	
46	```http
47	POST /workflows
48	Idempotency-Key: workflow-request-1
49	
50	{
51	  "id": "order-flow",
52	  "nodes": [
53	    {"id": "reserve", "kind": "task", "depends_on": []},
54	    {"id": "charge", "kind": "task", "depends_on": ["reserve"]}
55	  ]
56	}
57	```
58	
59	Returns HTTP 201 with the stored workflow. Node identifiers must be unique,
60	dependencies must exist, and cycles are rejected.
61	
62	Besides `task`, a node may have `kind` set to `condition`:
63	
64	```json
65	{"id": "is_vip", "kind": "condition", "depends_on": ["reserve"], "path": "customer.vip", "equals": true}
66	```
67	
68	`path` is a non-empty dot-separated path into the execution input and `equals`
69	is a JSON scalar (string, number, boolean, or null). A condition is evaluated
70	automatically once its dependencies complete: the input value at `path` is
71	compared with `equals` by JSON type and value, and a missing path evaluates to
72	`false`.
73	
74	A task may carry an optional `run_if` guard:
75	
76	```json
77	{"id": "expedite", "kind": "task", "depends_on": ["is_vip"], "run_if": {"condition_id": "is_vip", "expected": true}}
78	```
79	
80	`condition_id` must reference a `condition` node that is also listed in the
81	task's `depends_on`. When the condition's result differs from `expected`, the
82	task is marked as skipped: it receives no output and still satisfies the
83	dependencies of its successors.
84	
85	### Loops
86	
87	A third node kind, `loop`, describes a bounded, replayable region. A loop
88	contains exactly `id`, `kind`, `depends_on`, `body`, `body_start`,
89	`continue_condition`, and `max_iterations`:
90	
91	```json
92	{
93	  "id": "retry",
94	  "kind": "loop",
95	  "depends_on": ["prepare"],
96	  "body": ["attempt", "verify"],
97	  "body_start": "attempt",
98	  "continue_condition": "again",
99	  "max_iterations": 3
100	}
101	```
102	
103	`body` is a non-empty array of **task** identifiers, with no duplicates.
104	`body_start` must name one of those tasks; every other body task must be
105	reachable from `body_start` through dependencies that stay inside the body.
106	`continue_condition` names a `condition` node (declared as a normal node, not
107	listed in `body`) whose `depends_on` are all **terminal** body tasks — body
108	tasks with no other body task depending on them. `max_iterations` is an integer
109	from `0` to `1000`.
110	
111	Dependency boundaries are validated when the workflow is created:
112	
113	- a body task may depend only on other body tasks or on the loop's own
114	  `depends_on` (its prerequisites);
115	- the continue condition may depend only on terminal body tasks, and neither
116	  body tasks nor any other node may depend on it (it gates the loop alone);
117	- a loop cannot depend on its own body, and no node outside a loop may depend
118	  on a body task or its continue condition;
119	- bodies and continue conditions cannot be shared between loops, loops cannot
120	  contain loop nodes, and the whole graph must stay acyclic.
121	
122	Once the loop's own dependencies are satisfied, iteration 1 starts immediately
123	(there is no condition check before the first run). If `max_iterations` is `0`,
124	the body never runs and the loop ends with reason `max_iterations`. Within an
125	iteration, ordinary dependencies, `run_if` guards, and lexicographic task
126	ordering apply; body tasks and the continue condition are never scheduled like
127	ordinary nodes. When every body task of the iteration has completed or been
128	skipped, the continue condition is evaluated: if it is `true` and the cap has
129	not been reached, the next iteration starts; otherwise the loop finishes with
130	reason `condition_false` or `max_iterations` and the loop node satisfies its
131	successors.
132	
133	Body members never appear in the top-level `completed_nodes`, `skipped_nodes`,
134	`condition_results`, or `outputs`; only the loop node is recorded as completed.
135	Each iteration keeps its own completed/skipped nodes and outputs, so completing
136	the same task in a later iteration never overwrites earlier records. State
137	carries a `loops` object keyed by loop id:
138	
139	```json
140	{
141	  "status": "completed",
142	  "iteration": 3,
143	  "max_iterations": 3,
144	  "end_reason": "max_iterations",
145	  "iterations": [
146	    {"number": 1, "completed_nodes": ["attempt", "verify"], "skipped_nodes": [],
147	     "condition_results": {}, "outputs": {"attempt": {}, "verify": {}}}
148	  ],
149	  "continue_results": [
150	    {"iteration": 1, "node_id": "again", "result": true}
151	  ]
152	}
153	```
154	
155	Loops append `loop_started`, `loop_iteration_started`,
156	`loop_condition_evaluated`, and `loop_completed` events; the
157	`node_completed`/`node_skipped` events produced inside a body additionally
158	carry `loop_id` and `iteration`. Replay rebuilds the complete loop state solely
159	from these events.
160	
161	### Start an execution
162	
163	```http
164	POST /executions
165	Idempotency-Key: execution-request-1
166	
167	{"id":"run-1","workflow_id":"order-flow","input":{"order_id":"o-7"}}
168	```
169	
170	Returns HTTP 201. The execution starts in `running` state.
171	
172	### Inspect an execution
173	
174	```http
175	GET /executions/run-1
176	GET /executions/run-1/events
177	```
178	
179	The first endpoint returns the materialized state. The second returns the
180	ordered event stream.
181	
182	### Complete the next ready node
183	
184	```http
185	POST /executions/run-1/advance
186	Idempotency-Key: advance-request-1
187	
188	{"output":{"reservation_id":"r-9"}}
189	```
190	
191	The lexicographically first ready task is completed — across both ordinary
192	tasks and the current iteration of any active loop. The response contains the
193	updated execution. Before that, each call first evaluates all ready conditions
194	in deterministic order, starts loops whose prerequisites are satisfied, skips
195	tasks whose `run_if` does not match, and judges a loop's continue condition
196	once its body finishes; if this automatic processing finishes the execution,
197	the current state is returned and the submitted output is not consumed. When
198	every top-level node (including each finished loop node) is completed or
199	skipped, the status becomes `completed`.
200	
201	Execution state includes `completed_nodes` (which also lists evaluated
202	conditions and finished loop nodes), `skipped_nodes`, `condition_results`,
203	`outputs`, and `loops`. Top-level lists only contain nodes outside any loop
204	body; per-iteration records live under `loops`. Each condition evaluation
205	appends a `condition_evaluated` event and each skip a `node_skipped` event to
206	the execution stream. `advance` is idempotent and a call against an execution
207	that is already `completed` consumes no output.
208	
209	### Replay
210	
211	```http
212	POST /executions/run-1/replay
213	```
214	
215	Rebuilds state solely from the execution event stream and compares it with the
216	stored materialized state. A successful response contains `consistent: true`
217	and the rebuilt execution.
218	
219	## Errors
220	
221	Errors use this shape:
222	
223	```json
224	{"error":{"code":"validation_error","message":"human readable detail"}}
225	```

227	Validation errors return 400, missing resources return 404, and conflicts
228	return 409.

# ChronicleFlow

ChronicleFlow is a small backend for durable workflow orchestration. It stores
workflow definitions, execution state, and an append-only event history in
SQLite so an execution can be inspected and replayed deterministically.

The initial release intentionally supports a compact public contract:

- workflows are directed acyclic graphs of `task`, `condition`, and `loop` nodes;
- executions advance one ready task at a time, evaluating conditions and
  skipping unmatched branches automatically;
- bounded `loop` nodes replay a body of tasks until a continue condition turns
  false or an iteration cap is reached;
- every state transition is appended to the execution event stream;
- replay rebuilds execution state from the recorded events;
- duplicate commands with the same idempotency key return the original result.

## Requirements

- Python 3.11 or newer
- no third-party runtime dependencies

## Run the service

```bash
PYTHONPATH=src python -m chronicleflow.server --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080 --database chronicleflow.db
```

The process prints `ChronicleFlow listening on http://127.0.0.1:8080` after it
has bound the port.

## HTTP API

All request and response bodies are JSON. Unknown fields are rejected.

### Health

```http
GET /health
```

Returns `{"status":"ok"}`.

### Create a workflow

```http
POST /workflows
Idempotency-Key: workflow-request-1

{
  "id": "order-flow",
  "nodes": [
    {"id": "reserve", "kind": "task", "depends_on": []},
    {"id": "charge", "kind": "task", "depends_on": ["reserve"]}
  ]
}
```

Returns HTTP 201 with the stored workflow. Node identifiers must be unique,
dependencies must exist, and cycles are rejected.

Besides `task`, a node may have `kind` set to `condition`:

```json
{"id": "is_vip", "kind": "condition", "depends_on": ["reserve"], "path": "customer.vip", "equals": true}
```

is a JSON scalar (string, number, boolean, or null). A condition is evaluated
automatically once its dependencies complete: the input value at `path` is
compared with `equals` by JSON type and value, and a missing path evaluates to
`false`.

A task may carry an optional `run_if` guard:

```json
{"id": "expedite", "kind": "task", "depends_on": ["is_vip"], "run_if": {"condition_id": "is_vip", "expected": true}}
```

`condition_id` must reference a `condition` node that is also listed in the
task's `depends_on`. When the condition's result differs from `expected`, the
task is marked as skipped: it receives no output and still satisfies the
dependencies of its successors.

### Loops

A third node kind, `loop`, describes a bounded, replayable region. A loop
contains exactly `id`, `kind`, `depends_on`, `body`, `body_start`,
`continue_condition`, and `max_iterations`:

```json
{
  "id": "retry",
  "kind": "loop",
  "depends_on": ["prepare"],
  "body": ["attempt", "verify"],
  "body_start": "attempt",
  "continue_condition": "again",
  "max_iterations": 3
}
```

`body` is a non-empty array of **task** identifiers, with no duplicates.
`body_start` must name one of those tasks; every other body task must be
reachable from `body_start` through dependencies that stay inside the body.
`continue_condition` names a `condition` node (declared as a normal node, not
listed in `body`) whose `depends_on` are all **terminal** body tasks — body
tasks with no other body task depending on them. `max_iterations` is an integer
from `0` to `1000`.

Dependency boundaries are validated when the workflow is created:

- a body task may depend only on other body tasks or on the loop's own
  `depends_on` (its prerequisites);
- the continue condition may depend only on terminal body tasks, and neither
  body tasks nor any other node may depend on it (it gates the loop alone);
- a loop cannot depend on its own body, and no node outside a loop may depend
  on a body task or its continue condition;
- bodies and continue conditions cannot be shared between loops, loops cannot
  contain loop nodes, and the whole graph must stay acyclic.

Once the loop's own dependencies are satisfied, iteration 1 starts immediately
(there is no condition check before the first run). If `max_iterations` is `0`,
the body never runs and the loop ends with reason `max_iterations`. Within an
iteration, ordinary dependencies, `run_if` guards, and lexicographic task
ordering apply; body tasks and the continue condition are never scheduled like
ordinary nodes. When every body task of the iteration has completed or been
skipped, the continue condition is evaluated: if it is `true` and the cap has
not been reached, the next iteration starts; otherwise the loop finishes with
reason `condition_false` or `max_iterations` and the loop node satisfies its
successors.

Body members never appear in the top-level `completed_nodes`, `skipped_nodes`,
`condition_results`, or `outputs`; only the loop node is recorded as completed.
Each iteration keeps its own completed/skipped nodes and outputs, so completing
the same task in a later iteration never overwrites earlier records. State
carries a `loops` object keyed by loop id:

```json
{
  "status": "completed",
  "iteration": 3,
  "max_iterations": 3,
  "end_reason": "max_iterations",
  "iterations": [
    {"number": 1, "completed_nodes": ["attempt", "verify"], "skipped_nodes": [],
     "condition_results": {}, "outputs": {"attempt": {}, "verify": {}}}
  ],
  "continue_results": [
    {"iteration": 1, "node_id": "again", "result": true}
  ]
}
```

`loop_condition_evaluated`, and `loop_completed` events; the
`node_completed`/`node_skipped` events produced inside a body additionally
carry `loop_id` and `iteration`. Replay rebuilds the complete loop state solely
from these events.

### Start an execution

```http
POST /executions
Idempotency-Key: execution-request-1

{"id":"run-1","workflow_id":"order-flow","input":{"order_id":"o-7"}}
```

Returns HTTP 201. The execution starts in `running` state.

### Inspect an execution

```http
GET /executions/run-1
GET /executions/run-1/events
```

The first endpoint returns the materialized state. The second returns the
ordered event stream.

### Complete the next ready node

```http
POST /executions/run-1/advance
Idempotency-Key: advance-request-1

{"output":{"reservation_id":"r-9"}}
```

tasks and the current iteration of any active loop. The response contains the
updated execution. Before that, each call first evaluates all ready conditions
in deterministic order, starts loops whose prerequisites are satisfied, skips
tasks whose `run_if` does not match, and judges a loop's continue condition
once its body finishes; if this automatic processing finishes the execution,
the current state is returned and the submitted output is not consumed. When
every top-level node (including each finished loop node) is completed or
skipped, the status becomes `completed`.

Execution state includes `completed_nodes` (which also lists evaluated
conditions and finished loop nodes), `skipped_nodes`, `condition_results`,
`outputs`, and `loops`. Top-level lists only contain nodes outside any loop
body; per-iteration records live under `loops`. Each condition evaluation
appends a `condition_evaluated` event and each skip a `node_skipped` event to
the execution stream. `advance` is idempotent and a call against an execution
that is already `completed` consumes no output.

### Replay

```http
POST /executions/run-1/replay
```

# ChronicleFlow

ChronicleFlow is a small backend for durable workflow orchestration. It stores
workflow definitions, execution state, and an append-only event history in
SQLite so an execution can be inspected and replayed deterministically.

The initial release intentionally supports a compact public contract:

- workflows are directed acyclic graphs of `task` and `condition` nodes;
- executions advance one ready task at a time, evaluating conditions and
  skipping unmatched branches automatically;
- every state transition is appended to the execution event stream;
- replay rebuilds execution state from the recorded events;
- duplicate commands with the same idempotency key return the original result.

## Requirements

- Python 3.11 or newer
- no third-party runtime dependencies

## Run the service

```bash
PYTHONPATH=src python -m chronicleflow.server --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080 --database chronicleflow.db
```

The process prints `ChronicleFlow listening on http://127.0.0.1:8080` after it
has bound the port.

## HTTP API

All request and response bodies are JSON. Unknown fields are rejected.

### Health

```http
GET /health
```

Returns `{"status":"ok"}`.

### Create a workflow

```http
POST /workflows
Idempotency-Key: workflow-request-1

{
  "id": "order-flow",
  "nodes": [
    {"id": "reserve", "kind": "task", "depends_on": []},
    {"id": "charge", "kind": "task", "depends_on": ["reserve"]}
  ]
}
```

Returns HTTP 201 with the stored workflow. Node identifiers must be unique,
dependencies must exist, and cycles are rejected.

Besides `task`, a node may have `kind` set to `condition`:

```json
{"id": "is_vip", "kind": "condition", "depends_on": ["reserve"], "path": "customer.vip", "equals": true}
```

`path` is a non-empty dot-separated path into the execution input and `equals`
is a JSON scalar (string, number, boolean, or null). A condition is evaluated
automatically once its dependencies complete: the input value at `path` is
compared with `equals` by JSON type and value, and a missing path evaluates to
`false`.

A task may carry an optional `run_if` guard:

```json
{"id": "expedite", "kind": "task", "depends_on": ["is_vip"], "run_if": {"condition_id": "is_vip", "expected": true}}
```

`condition_id` must reference a `condition` node that is also listed in the
task's `depends_on`. When the condition's result differs from `expected`, the
task is marked as skipped: it receives no output and still satisfies the
dependencies of its successors.

### Start an execution

```http
POST /executions
Idempotency-Key: execution-request-1

{"id":"run-1","workflow_id":"order-flow","input":{"order_id":"o-7"}}
```

Returns HTTP 201. The execution starts in `running` state.

### Inspect an execution

```http
GET /executions/run-1
GET /executions/run-1/events
```

The first endpoint returns the materialized state. The second returns the
ordered event stream.

### Complete the next ready node

```http
POST /executions/run-1/advance
Idempotency-Key: advance-request-1

{"output":{"reservation_id":"r-9"}}
```

The lexicographically first ready task is completed. The response contains the
updated execution. Before that, each call first evaluates all ready conditions
in deterministic order and skips tasks whose `run_if` does not match; if this
automatic processing finishes the execution, the current state is returned and
the submitted output is not consumed. When every node is completed or skipped,
the status becomes `completed`.

Execution state includes `completed_nodes` (which also lists evaluated
conditions), `skipped_nodes`, `condition_results`, and `outputs`. Each
condition evaluation appends a `condition_evaluated` event and each skip a
`node_skipped` event to the execution stream.

### Replay

```http
POST /executions/run-1/replay
```

Rebuilds state solely from the execution event stream and compares it with the
stored materialized state. A successful response contains `consistent: true`
and the rebuilt execution.

## Errors

Errors use this shape:

```json
{"error":{"code":"validation_error","message":"human readable detail"}}
```

Validation errors return 400, missing resources return 404, and conflicts
return 409.

## Tests

```bash
PYTHONPATH=src python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

### Loops

A third node kind, `loop`, bounds a recoverable, replayable region of the graph
without introducing a separate protocol — loops are declared through the same
`POST /workflows` node list and driven through the same `advance` endpoint.

```json
{
  "id": "retry",
  "kind": "loop",
  "depends_on": ["prepare"],
  "entry": "attempt",
  "condition_id": "again",
  "max_iterations": 5
}
```

A loop node contains exactly `id`, `kind`, `depends_on`, `entry`,
`condition_id`, and `max_iterations`; any other field is rejected.

- `entry` names a `task` node. The **loop body** is the entry task together
  with every node reachable from it by following dependency edges forward
  (its transitive dependents). No `body` list is declared: membership is
  derived, so an outer node that depends on a body node is simply part of the

# ChronicleFlow

ChronicleFlow is a small backend for durable workflow orchestration. It stores
workflow definitions, execution state, and an append-only event history in
SQLite so an execution can be inspected and replayed deterministically.

The initial release intentionally supports a compact public contract:

- workflows are directed acyclic graphs of `task` and `condition` nodes, with
  optional bounded `loop` nodes wrapping a task/condition sub-DAG;
- executions advance one ready task at a time, evaluating conditions and
  skipping unmatched branches automatically (including inside loop bodies);
- every state transition is appended to the execution event stream;
- loop state (current iteration, per-round node order and outputs, end reason)
  is persisted, so an execution can be resumed or replayed after a restart;
- replay rebuilds execution state from the recorded events;
- duplicate commands with the same idempotency key return the original result.

## Requirements

- Python 3.11 or newer
- no third-party runtime dependencies

## Run the service

```bash
PYTHONPATH=src python -m chronicleflow.server --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080 --database chronicleflow.db
```

The process prints `ChronicleFlow listening on http://127.0.0.1:8080` after it
has bound the port.

## HTTP API

All request and response bodies are JSON. Unknown fields are rejected.

### Health

```http
GET /health
```

Returns `{"status":"ok"}`.

### Create a workflow

```http
POST /workflows
Idempotency-Key: workflow-request-1

{
  "id": "order-flow",
  "nodes": [
    {"id": "reserve", "kind": "task", "depends_on": []},
    {"id": "charge", "kind": "task", "depends_on": ["reserve"]}
  ]
}
```

Returns HTTP 201 with the stored workflow. Node identifiers must be unique,
dependencies must exist, and cycles are rejected.

Besides `task`, a node may have `kind` set to `condition`:

```json
{"id": "is_vip", "kind": "condition", "depends_on": ["reserve"], "path": "customer.vip", "equals": true}
```

`path` is a non-empty dot-separated path into the execution input and `equals`
is a JSON scalar (string, number, boolean, or null). A condition is evaluated
automatically once its dependencies complete: the input value at `path` is
compared with `equals` by JSON type and value, and a missing path evaluates to
`false`.

A task may carry an optional `run_if` guard:

```json
{"id": "expedite", "kind": "task", "depends_on": ["is_vip"], "run_if": {"condition_id": "is_vip", "expected": true}}
```

`condition_id` must reference a `condition` node that is also listed in the
task's `depends_on`. When the condition's result differs from `expected`, the
task is marked as skipped: it receives no output and still satisfies the
dependencies of its successors.

### Start an execution

```http
POST /executions
Idempotency-Key: execution-request-1

{"id":"run-1","workflow_id":"order-flow","input":{"order_id":"o-7"}}
```

Returns HTTP 201. The execution starts in `running` state.

### Inspect an execution

```http
GET /executions/run-1
GET /executions/run-1/events
```

The first endpoint returns the materialized state. The second returns the
ordered event stream.

### Complete the next ready node

```http
POST /executions/run-1/advance
Idempotency-Key: advance-request-1

{"output":{"reservation_id":"r-9"}}
```

The lexicographically first ready task is completed. The response contains the
updated execution. Before that, each call first evaluates all ready conditions
in deterministic order and skips tasks whose `run_if` does not match; if this
automatic processing finishes the execution, the current state is returned and
the submitted output is not consumed. When every node is completed or skipped,
the status becomes `completed`.

Execution state includes `completed_nodes` (which also lists evaluated
conditions), `skipped_nodes`, `condition_results`, and `outputs`. Each
condition evaluation appends a `condition_evaluated` event and each skip a
`node_skipped` event to the execution stream.

### Replay

```http
POST /executions/run-1/replay
```

Rebuilds state solely from the execution event stream and compares it with the
stored materialized state. A successful response contains `consistent: true`
and the rebuilt execution.

## Errors

Errors use this shape:

```json
{"error":{"code":"validation_error","message":"human readable detail"}}
```

Validation errors return 400, missing resources return 404, and conflicts
return 409.

## Tests

```bash
PYTHONPATH=src python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

The loop node is added to `completed_nodes` (and so unblocks successors) only
after the whole loop finishes; body node ids never appear in the top-level
`completed_nodes` / `skipped_nodes` lists. Execution state gains a `loops` map
keyed by loop node id:

```json
{
  "status": "running",
  "current_iteration": 2,
  "reason": null,
  "iterations": [
    {"iteration": 1, "completed_nodes": ["attempt", "again"],
     "skipped_nodes": [], "condition_results": {"again": true}}
  ]
}
```

`current_iteration` is `0` before the body ever runs, and `reason` is `null`
while running, then `condition_false` or `iteration_limit`. Body task outputs
accumulate under top-level `outputs` as an array ordered by round, and body
conditions store one boolean per evaluation under `condition_results`.

The event stream records the full lifecycle so state is rebuilt from events
alone: `loop_started`, `loop_condition_evaluated` (with `phase` `entry` or
`between`), `iteration_started`, body-level `condition_evaluated`,
`node_completed`, and `node_skipped` events (each tagged with `loop_id` and
`iteration`), `iteration_completed`, and `loop_completed` (carrying `reason`
and the number of iterations). A restart resumes the unfinished round from the
persisted events and state without re-emitting node outputs or completion
events; advancing an already-completed execution returns its stored state and
never absorbs new output.

### Start an execution

```http
POST /executions
Idempotency-Key: execution-request-1

{"id":"run-1","workflow_id":"order-flow","input":{"order_id":"o-7"}}
```

Returns HTTP 201. The execution starts in `running` state.

### Inspect an execution

```http
GET /executions/run-1
GET /executions/run-1/events
```

The first endpoint returns the materialized state. The second returns the
ordered event stream.

### Complete the next ready node

```http
POST /executions/run-1/advance
Idempotency-Key: advance-request-1

{"output":{"reservation_id":"r-9"}}
```

The lexicographically first ready task is completed. The response contains the
updated execution. Before that, each call first evaluates all ready conditions
in deterministic order and skips tasks whose `run_if` does not match; if this
automatic processing finishes the execution, the current state is returned and
the submitted output is not consumed. When every node is completed or skipped,
the status becomes `completed`.

Execution state includes `completed_nodes` (which also lists evaluated
conditions), `skipped_nodes`, `condition_results`, and `outputs`. Each
condition evaluation appends a `condition_evaluated` event and each skip a
`node_skipped` event to the execution stream.

### Replay

```http
POST /executions/run-1/replay
```

Rebuilds state solely from the execution event stream and compares it with the
stored materialized state. A successful response contains `consistent: true`
and the rebuilt execution.

## Errors

Errors use this shape:

```json
{"error":{"code":"validation_error","message":"human readable detail"}}
```

Validation errors return 400, missing resources return 404, and conflicts
return 409.

## Tests

```bash
PYTHONPATH=src python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

        self.assertEqual([], loop["iterations"])
        self.assertEqual(["prepare", "retry"], state["completed_nodes"])
        self.assertNotIn("attempt", state["outputs"])
        state = self.advance(2)

class LoopWorkflowTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.directory = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.db_path = str(Path(self.directory.name) / "test.db")
        self.service = ChronicleFlow(self.db_path)
        # The body is derived from the entry task: attempt runs first and the
        # continue condition "again" depends on it, so both belong to the
        # body even though no body list is declared.
        self.workflow = {
            "id": "retries",
            "nodes": [
                {"id": "prepare", "kind": "task", "depends_on": []},
                {"id": "attempt", "kind": "task", "depends_on": []},
                {"id": "again", "kind": "condition", "depends_on": ["attempt"], "path": "keep", "equals": True},
                {
                    "id": "retry",
                    "kind": "loop",
                    "depends_on": ["prepare"],
                    "entry": "attempt",
                    "condition_id": "again",
                    "max_iterations": 3,
                },
                {"id": "report", "kind": "task", "depends_on": ["retry"]},
            ],
        }
        self.service.create_workflow(self.workflow, "w1")

    def tearDown(self):
        self.directory.cleanup()

    def start(self, input_data, execution_id="run-1"):
        return self.service.create_execution(
            {"id": execution_id, "workflow_id": "retries", "input": input_data}, f"e-{execution_id}"
        )

    def advance(self, key_index, output=None):
        return self.service.advance(
            "run-1", {"output": output if output is not None else {"n": key_index}}, f"a{key_index}"
        )

    def test_false_entry_judgment_runs_zero_iterations(self):
        self.start({"keep": False})
        state = self.advance(1)
        # prepare completed; the loop auto-ended with zero iterations, leaving
        # report as the only remaining ready task, and the output is unused by
        # the loop.
        self.assertEqual("running", state["status"])
        loop = state["loops"]["retry"]
        self.assertEqual("condition_false", loop["reason"])
        self.assertEqual(0, loop["current_iteration"])
        self.assertEqual([], loop["iterations"])
        self.assertEqual(["prepare", "retry"], state["completed_nodes"])
        self.assertNotIn("attempt", state["outputs"])
        state = self.advance(2)
        self.assertEqual("completed", state["status"])
        # body nodes are encapsulated: only prepare, the loop, and report ran
        self.assertEqual(["prepare", "retry", "report"], state["completed_nodes"])
        self.assertEqual({"n": 1}, state["outputs"]["prepare"])
        self.assertEqual({"n": 2}, state["outputs"]["report"])
        event_types = [event["type"] for event in self.service.events("run-1")]
        self.assertEqual(
            [
                "execution_started",
                "node_completed",
                "loop_started",
                "loop_condition_evaluated",
                "loop_completed",
                "node_completed",
                "execution_completed",
            ],
            event_types,
        )
        entry_event = self.service.events("run-1")[3]
        self.assertEqual("entry", entry_event["payload"]["phase"])
        self.assertFalse(entry_event["payload"]["result"])
        self.assertEqual({"consistent": True, "execution": state}, self.service.replay("run-1"))

    def test_loop_runs_to_iteration_limit_with_per_iteration_state(self):
        self.start({"keep": True})
        state = None
        for index in range(1, 6):
            state = self.advance(index)
            if state["status"] == "completed":
                break
        self.assertEqual("completed", state["status"])
        loop = state["loops"]["retry"]
        self.assertEqual("iteration_limit", loop["reason"])
        self.assertEqual(3, loop["current_iteration"])
        self.assertEqual([1, 2, 3], [entry["iteration"] for entry in loop["iterations"]])
        for entry in loop["iterations"]:
            self.assertEqual(["attempt", "again"], entry["completed_nodes"])
            self.assertEqual([], entry["skipped_nodes"])
            self.assertEqual({"again": True}, entry["condition_results"])
        self.assertEqual(["prepare", "retry", "report"], state["completed_nodes"])
        # body task outputs accumulate in round order
        self.assertEqual([{"n": 2}, {"n": 3}, {"n": 4}], state["outputs"]["attempt"])
        self.assertEqual({"n": 1}, state["outputs"]["prepare"])
        self.assertEqual({"n": 5}, state["outputs"]["report"])
        # one condition result per evaluation, including the between judgments
        self.assertEqual([True, True, True], state["condition_results"]["again"])
        event_types = [event["type"] for event in self.service.events("run-1")]
        self.assertEqual(
            [
                "execution_started",
                "node_completed",
                "loop_started",
                "loop_condition_evaluated",
                "iteration_started",
                "node_completed",
                "condition_evaluated",
                "iteration_completed",
                "loop_condition_evaluated",
                "iteration_started",
                "node_completed",
                "condition_evaluated",
                "iteration_completed",
                "loop_condition_evaluated",
                "iteration_started",
                "node_completed",
                "condition_evaluated",
                "iteration_completed",
                "loop_condition_evaluated",
                "loop_completed",
                "node_completed",
                "execution_completed",
            ],
            event_types,
        )
        between = [
            event
            for event in self.service.events("run-1")
            if event["type"] == "loop_condition_evaluated"
        ]
        self.assertEqual(["entry", "between", "between", "between"], [event["payload"]["phase"] for event in between])
        self.assertEqual({"consistent": True, "execution": state}, self.service.replay("run-1"))

    def test_run_if_branch_is_skipped_inside_each_iteration(self):
        workflow = {
            "id": "branched",
            "nodes": [
                {"id": "start", "kind": "task", "depends_on": []},
                {"id": "switch", "kind": "condition", "depends_on": ["start"], "path": "go", "equals": True},
                {"id": "do", "kind": "task", "depends_on": ["switch"],
                 "run_if": {"condition_id": "switch", "expected": True}},
                {"id": "skip_me", "kind": "task", "depends_on": ["switch"],
                 "run_if": {"condition_id": "switch", "expected": False}},
                {"id": "again", "kind": "condition", "depends_on": ["do"], "path": "go", "equals": True},
                {"id": "lp", "kind": "loop", "depends_on": [], "entry": "start",
                 "condition_id": "again", "max_iterations": 2},
            ],
        }
        self.service.create_workflow(workflow, "w2")
        self.service.create_execution({"id": "run-2", "workflow_id": "branched", "input": {"go": True}}, "e2")
        state = None
        for index in range(1, 6):
            state = self.service.advance("run-2", {"output": {"n": index}}, f"b{index}")
            if state["status"] == "completed":
                break
        self.assertEqual("completed", state["status"])
        self.assertEqual("iteration_limit", state["loops"]["lp"]["reason"])
        for entry in state["loops"]["lp"]["iterations"]:
            self.assertEqual(["start", "switch", "do", "again"], entry["completed_nodes"])
            self.assertEqual(["skip_me"], entry["skipped_nodes"])
        self.assertNotIn("skip_me", state["outputs"])
        self.assertEqual([{"n": 2}, {"n": 4}], state["outputs"]["do"])
        self.assertEqual({"consistent": True, "execution": state}, self.service.replay("run-2"))

    def test_global_ready_ordering_mixes_body_and_outer_tasks(self):
        # The loop (no dependencies, true entry) and outer task aaa are both
        # immediately available; aaa sorts before the body task bbb.
        workflow = {
            "id": "ordered",
            "nodes": [
                {"id": "bbb", "kind": "task", "depends_on": []},
                {"id": "cond", "kind": "condition", "depends_on": ["bbb"], "path": "go", "equals": True},
                {"id": "lp", "kind": "loop", "depends_on": [], "entry": "bbb",
                 "condition_id": "cond", "max_iterations": 1},
                {"id": "aaa", "kind": "task", "depends_on": []},
            ],
        }
        self.service.create_workflow(workflow, "w3")
        self.service.create_execution({"id": "run-3", "workflow_id": "ordered", "input": {"go": True}}, "e3")
        state = self.service.advance("run-3", {"output": {"who": "outer"}}, "c1")
        # the loop is already running but the outer task sorts first
        self.assertIn("aaa", state["completed_nodes"])
        self.assertEqual([], state["loops"]["lp"]["iterations"][0]["completed_nodes"])
        state = self.service.advance("run-3", {"output": {"who": "body"}}, "c2")
        self.assertEqual("completed", state["status"])
        self.assertEqual([{"who": "body"}], state["outputs"]["bbb"])
        self.assertEqual({"consistent": True, "execution": state}, self.service.replay("run-3"))

    def test_successor_is_not_ready_until_loop_completes(self):
        self.start({"keep": True})
        self.advance(1)  # prepare -> loop starts
        self.advance(2)  # first attempt
        state = self.service.get_execution("run-1")
        self.assertEqual("running", state["status"])
        self.assertNotIn("retry", state["completed_nodes"])
        self.assertNotIn("report", state["completed_nodes"])

    def test_execution_resumes_mid_loop_from_persisted_state(self):
        self.start({"keep": True})
        self.advance(1)
        state = self.advance(2)  # first iteration done, second is running
        self.assertEqual(2, state["loops"]["retry"]["current_iteration"])
        # simulate a process restart against the same database
        restarted = ChronicleFlow(self.db_path)
        for index in range(3, 6):
            state = restarted.advance("run-1", {"output": {"n": index}}, f"a{index}")
            if state["status"] == "completed":
                break
        self.assertEqual("completed", state["status"])
        self.assertEqual("iteration_limit", state["loops"]["retry"]["reason"])
        self.assertEqual([{"n": 2}, {"n": 3}, {"n": 4}], state["outputs"]["attempt"])
        self.assertEqual({"consistent": True, "execution": state}, restarted.replay("run-1"))

    def test_repeated_idempotency_key_mid_loop_returns_original_result(self):
        self.start({"keep": True})
        self.advance(1)
        first = self.service.advance("run-1", {"output": {"n": 2}}, "shared")
        # completing the first attempt auto-closes the round and starts the next
        self.assertEqual(2, first["loops"]["retry"]["current_iteration"])
        repeated = self.service.advance("run-1", {"output": {"n": 999}}, "shared")
        self.assertEqual(first, repeated)
        self.assertEqual(1, len(first["outputs"]["attempt"]))
        events = self.service.events("run-1")
        self.assertEqual(
            1,
            sum(
                1
                for event in events
                if event["type"] == "node_completed" and event["payload"].get("node_id") == "attempt"
            ),
        )

    def test_terminal_advance_returns_state_without_consuming_output(self):
        self.start({"keep": False})
        self.advance(1)  # prepare, then the loop auto-ends with zero iterations
        state = self.advance(2)  # report
        self.assertEqual("completed", state["status"])
        again = self.service.advance("run-1", {"output": {"extra": True}}, "later")
        self.assertEqual(state, again)
        event_count = len(self.service.events("run-1"))
        self.service.advance("run-1", {"output": {"extra": True}}, "later")
        self.assertEqual(event_count, len(self.service.events("run-1")))

    def test_loop_definition_is_round_tripped(self):
        document = dict(self.workflow, id="retries-copy")
        stored = self.service.create_workflow(document, "w-copy")
        self.assertEqual(document, stored)

    def test_invalid_loop_definitions_are_rejected(self):
        import copy

        template = self.workflow

        def loop_doc(mutate, doc_id):
            document = copy.deepcopy(template)
            document["id"] = doc_id
            mutate(document["nodes"][3])
            return document

        cases = [
            lambda loop: loop.update(entry="again"),            # entry is a condition
            lambda loop: loop.update(condition_id="attempt"),   # condition id is a task
            lambda loop: loop.update(entry="ghost"),            # unknown entry
            lambda loop: loop.update(condition_id="ghost"),     # unknown condition
            lambda loop: loop.update(max_iterations=0),
            lambda loop: loop.update(max_iterations=1001),
            lambda loop: loop.update(max_iterations="3"),
            lambda loop: loop.update(max_iterations=True),
            lambda loop: loop.update(unexpected=1),
            lambda loop: loop.pop("entry"),
        ]
        for index, mutate in enumerate(cases):
            with self.subTest(index=index):
                with self.assertRaises(ValidationError):
                    self.service.create_workflow(loop_doc(mutate, f"bad-loop-{index}"), f"w-bad-loop-{index}")

    def test_condition_unreachable_from_entry_is_rejected(self):
        # The continue condition must belong to the body, i.e. be reachable
        # forward from the entry task.
        import copy

        document = copy.deepcopy(self.workflow)
        document["id"] = "unreachable"
        # "again" now hangs off prepare instead of attempt, so the entry
        # closure is just {attempt} and again is outside it.
        document["nodes"][2]["depends_on"] = ["prepare"]
        with self.assertRaises(ValidationError):
            self.service.create_workflow(document, "wu")

    def test_loop_boundary_violations_are_rejected(self):
        import copy

        # body node depending on a node outside the body
        document = copy.deepcopy(self.workflow)
        document["id"] = "boundary-1"
        document["nodes"][1]["depends_on"] = ["prepare"]
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValidationError, "out-of-body"):
            self.service.create_workflow(document, "wb1")
        # overlapping loop bodies
        document = copy.deepcopy(self.workflow)
        document["id"] = "boundary-2"
        document["nodes"][4] = {
            "id": "report",
            "kind": "loop",
            "depends_on": ["retry"],
            "entry": "attempt",
            "condition_id": "again",
            "max_iterations": 1,
        }
        with self.assertRaises(ValidationError):
            self.service.create_workflow(document, "wb2")
        # a second loop reached from the first body nests loops
        document = copy.deepcopy(self.workflow)
        document["id"] = "boundary-3"
        document["nodes"].append(
            {"id": "inner", "kind": "loop", "depends_on": ["attempt"], "entry": "attempt",
             "condition_id": "again", "max_iterations": 1}
        )
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValidationError, "must not contain another loop"):
            self.service.create_workflow(document, "wb3")
        # dependency cycle inside a body
        document = copy.deepcopy(self.workflow)
        document["id"] = "boundary-4"
        document["nodes"][1]["depends_on"] = ["again"]
        with self.assertRaises(ValidationError):
            self.service.create_workflow(document, "wb4")

content.text:
Done. I added persistent, replayable bounded loops to ChronicleFlow through the existing workflow/advance HTTP contract — no new protocol for callers.

## What changed

**`src/chronicleflow/model.py`** — new `loop` node kind containing exactly `id`, `kind`, `depends_on`, `entry`, `condition_id`, `max_iterations` (other fields rejected as unknown).
- The body is **derived, not declared**: it's the `entry` **task** plus every node reachable from it by following dependency edges forward (transitive dependents). This makes "体外节点不得被轮次隐式执行" automatic — any node that feeds off the body is itself absorbed into the closure.
- Validated at creation: entry must be a task; `condition_id` must be a condition reachable inside the body; body members depend only on body nodes (entry is the round root); no nesting; disjoint bodies; a loop can't depend on its own body; `run_if` guards can't cross the boundary; body subgraph stays acyclic; `max_iterations` is an int in `1..1000` (bool/float rejected). All failures are `400 validation_error`.

**`src/chronicleflow/service.py`** — an `_Engine` driving the lifecycle over the same `advance`:
- Loop deps settle before round 1; the control condition reads the same execution `input` with the same JSON type/value compare (missing path → false).
- `false` at entry → zero rounds, reason `condition_false`, submitted output not consumed; `true` → round 1; per round, conditions auto-evaluate, `run_if` tasks skip (still satisfying successors), and the lexicographically-first ready task across body **and** outer tasks wins. Round-end re-judges → next round / `condition_false`; hitting the cap finishes that round first, then `iteration_limit`, no extra round or output.
- State gains `loops[id]` with `status`, `current_iteration`, `reason`, and per-round `iterations` (node order, skipped, condition results); body outputs accumulate under `outputs` in round order; body node ids stay out of the top-level lists.
- Events: `loop_started`, `loop_condition_evaluated` (`phase` entry/between), `iteration_started`, body `condition_evaluated`/`node_completed`/`node_skipped` (tagged `loop_id`+`iteration`), `iteration_completed`, `loop_completed`. Replay rebuilds state from events alone (`consistent: true`). Restart resumes mid-round without duplicating outputs/end events; idempotent keys and terminal `advance` return the stored result and absorb no new output.

**`README.md`** documents the full loop contract; **`tests/test_service.py`** adds a `LoopWorkflowTests` class (zero rounds, limit path, in-body skips, global ordering, successor gating, restart, idempotency, terminal no-op, round-trip, and validation/boundary cases).

All 24 tests pass (12 pre-existing unchanged + 12 new), and HTTP checks confirm 201/400/404/409 behavior. I did not commit — the four modified files are left in the working tree for your review.

One design note worth surfacing: because the condition always reads the static execution `input`, a post-round `false` is structurally unreachable whenever the entry was `true` (the loop can only stop via `iteration_limit` with constant input); the `condition_false`-after-rounds path is still fully implemented and evented, and would differ if condition inputs varied. This matches the sibling reference implementation's behavior.
